We've open-sourced our code for the purpose of the milestone. You can find it here: https://www.kaggle.com/code/jeroencottaar/taaf-duck-harness-kaggle

A more shareable verison (that didn't get the same lucky score) is here, we highly recommend working from this one: https://www.kaggle.com/code/jeroencottaar/taaf-duck-harness-kaggle-share

Tomorrow at 3 PM CEST we'll share a detailed technical writeup and several supporting materials, so stay tuned.
Thanks, these milestone shares will help in getting better scores on Arc3. Crazy how your solution solves many level 2 from public run. Great solution!
Awesome congratulations, i am excited on your work I also read some papers from your lab I think some of them might be useful in this competition
Same here Greg, and wow, you competed as well!

@gregkamradt Will this competition end here, or will it continue?

The highest score was supposed to be 1, but the top participant has already exceeded that value. Could you please explain how the competition will proceed from this point onward?

Good job!

Does it produce stable scores across different unmodified runs, or there's very high variance in the scores?
No, it's very unstable, ranging from 0.7 to 1.3.

congrats guys! Out of my 19 submissions 3 of my failed attempts were maybe 85-90% on the same path but only 25-30% ready for a submission… I ended up going a different route… boy do I wish I had stuck to that idea… anyways, can't wait to read the technical writeup!
Can i join your team if i make up to 2.5 score?
